title: The A2/A3 cube-to-vector bridge, through a two-slot GM workspace
surface: GMBuff(f32, [32, 16], slots=2) as the bridge; CvMutex(0, depth=1, src_end_pipe=Pipe.FIX, dst_end_pipe=Pipe.MTE2) with lock / ready / wait / free; GetSubBlockIdx() row ownership; matmul into L0C stored to GM and read back to UB with MTE2; muls on the vector side; kernel(mode="mix") from the a2 or a3 facade
study_for: Why this kernel exists at all: A5 can move an L0C accumulator straight into UB, and A2/A3 cannot. The result therefore goes out to GM and comes back, and the extra round trip is the whole difference between the two families' cube-to-vector handoff.

`CvMutex(..., src_end_pipe=Pipe.FIX, dst_end_pipe=Pipe.MTE2)` names the two pipes at the ends of the handoff: the fixpipe writing GM, MTE2 reading it back. That is what the mutex is ordering, and the slot is returned only after *both* vector readers have finished -- not after either one.

`GetSubBlockIdx() * 16` is how each vector participant finds its own half of a 32-row product. Both halves are compared together, and `check_domain` refuses a case where either half is all zero, since a participant whose result is zeros cannot be told from one that never ran.

Three beats over two slots means the third beat reuses the first slot, so the mutex has something to hold back. `compare` reports which beat and which half disagreed, because for this kernel that localizes the fault immediately.

The operands are integers in [-4, 4] with K = 16 and the vector side multiplies by two, so every result is an exact integer well inside FP32 -- which is what makes the byte comparison legitimate, and `check_domain` says so.
do_not_copy_when: You are on A5. The direct L0C-to-UB route exists there and this GM round trip is a cost you do not need; the A5 arrangement is a separate example with its own mutex and its own pipes.
You expect the slot back after one reader. Both vector participants read every slot here, and the mutex is what enforces that.
Your operands are not exactly representable. The byte comparison rests on that; ordinary data needs a tolerance and a reference that states one.
Your geometry is not 32x16x16 over three beats. The slot size, the subblock split and the reuse pattern are all sized for it.
